commands.author: paulcam206

target.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw does not currently have an official installable MXC sandbox backend for Windows hosts that can run sandboxed commands through Microsoft eXecution Containers. This leaves MXC-capable Windows environments without a first-party plugin path for ProcessContainer-backed execution and filesystem bridge operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an official OpenShell-style external `mxc` sandbox plugin package (`@openclaw/mxc-sandbox`) with Windows-only readiness checks, plugin-owned MXC SDK dependency ownership, ProcessContainer payload construction, a plugin-side launcher, host-backed filesystem bridge support, sandbox policy loading, and targeted tests.

The plugin source lives under `extensions/mxc`, but it is packaged as an installable plugin (`bundledDist: false`) so the MXC SDK/native dependency is owned by the plugin package instead of an unshipped bundled `node_modules` tree. The backend uses the stable current MXC `0.7.0-alpha` schema and keeps sandbox defaults conservative: curated environments, headless UI, per-exec temp directories, absolute binary overrides, host-derived Windows roots, read-only default workspace access for `none`/`ro`, protected skill overlays for `rw`, and fail-closed unsupported policy handling.

The latest remediation keeps the MXC read-only skill mount resolver plugin-local instead of exporting a new `openclaw/plugin-sdk/sandbox` helper only for this plugin. That preserves the current `>=2026.6.11` host/API floor without claiming a public SDK export that no shipped release tag currently contains.

## User Impact

Users on MXC-capable Windows hosts can install the official MXC sandbox plugin, restart the Gateway, configure `sandbox.backend: "mxc"`, and run OpenClaw sandboxed commands through MXC. Non-Windows or unsupported Windows hosts remain unaffected because the plugin stays dormant when readiness probes fail.

Install command:

```bash
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mxc-sandbox
```

## Evidence

CONTRIBUTING.md routing note: this PR follows the PR-template expectation for a feature/change by keeping visible related context, user impact, and validation evidence in the body. Upstream MXC config-transport tracking is now visible as Related: https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/626.
Current branch state:

- Current PR head after squash: `95f08788a0c1c3ede7814e74f7423b2e180aeedf`
- Current PR base after squash: `b81666ca6a04e5977dc565e205e36ae381c63d4b`
- PR branch is now one commit on top of current upstream `main`.
- Scope remains focused on the external MXC sandbox plugin and plugin/package metadata.
- Latest follow-up for comment `4910776193`: MXC now mirrors OpenShell by registering sandbox runtime hooks only during `api.registrationMode === "full"`; lightweight discovery, tool-discovery, setup, and CLI metadata registration paths stay side-effect-free.
- Protected skill overlay proof remains covered by MXC backend tests for both command execution and fs-bridge mutation paths under `workspaceAccess: "rw"`.

Focused/local validation:

- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `pnpm test:extension mxc -- --reporter=verbose` - passed.
- `pnpm test src\commands\sandbox.test.ts src\agents\sandbox\manage.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` - passed.
- `pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:changed:check` - passed.
- Previous package metadata/build validation remains relevant for unchanged packaging surfaces:
  - `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`
  - `pnpm test test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
  - `pnpm test:contracts:plugins`
  - `node scripts/check-src-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json`
  - `node scripts/check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json`
  - `node scripts/check-test-helper-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json`
  - `pnpm build`

MXC policy config follow-up proof:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/config.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/sandbox-policy-loader.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/mxc-backend.test.ts extensions/mxc/index.test.ts` - passed locally, 4 files / 58 tests.
- `pnpm plugins:inventory:check` - passed.
- `pnpm docs:map:check` - passed.
- Targeted `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 ...` for changed MXC/docs files - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- Crabbox static SSH Windows proof: `provider=ssh`, `lease=static_172-28-55-39`, target `windows-normal`, host `adminuser@172.28.55.39`; after `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, the same focused MXC Vitest command passed, 4 files / 58 tests, exit `0`, `leaseStopped=true`.

Post-squash validation:

- Squashed branch has exactly one commit over `upstream/main`: `95f08788a0 feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend`.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` - passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/config.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/sandbox-policy-loader.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/mxc-backend.test.ts extensions/mxc/index.test.ts` - passed locally, 4 files / 58 tests.
- `pnpm plugins:inventory:check` - passed.
- `pnpm docs:map:check` - passed.
- Targeted `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 ...` for changed MXC/docs files - passed.

AI review closeout:

- `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD --engine copilot` on commit `ebd884dd27` reported one P2 about `baselineContext` being unused; rejected as a false positive because `baselineContext` is used by the returned `buildExecSpec` closure for `createSandboxTempDir(baselineContext.hostEnv)` and `buildContainerConfig({ baselineContext, ... })`.
- Rejection proof: `node scripts\run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions\mxc\tsconfig.json extensions\mxc\src\mxc-backend.ts` passed.
- Earlier Copilot autoreview on the full branch bundle was not usable because the Copilot engine refused truncated input for the large existing PR diff, so the review was scoped to the new commit.

Windows install/load proof:
- Provider/lease: `ssh` / `static_172-26-197-87`
- Target: `windows-normal`
- SSH: `adminuser@172.26.197.87`
- Package built through the release packaging path (`scripts/lib/plugin-npm-runtime-build.mjs` plus `scripts/lib/plugin-npm-package-manifest.mjs --run ... npm pack`) so the `.tgz` includes compiled runtime output.
- Installed `@openclaw/mxc-sandbox@2026.6.11` from the generated package archive into isolated OpenClaw state.
- `openclaw plugins inspect mxc --runtime --json` loaded the plugin runtime successfully.
- Proof markers included:
  - `PROOF_INSTALLED_PACKAGE_NAME @openclaw/mxc-sandbox`
  - `PROOF_INSTALLED_PACKAGE_VERSION 2026.6.11`
  - `PROOF_INSTALLED_MIN_HOST >=2026.6.11`
  - `PROOF_INSTALLED_PLUGIN_API >=2026.6.11`
  - `PROOF_RUNTIME_LOAD_OK`
  - `PROOF_STATIC_WINDOWS_INSTALL_LOAD_OK`

Windows runtime proof and screenshot:

- Exact-head runtime proof on `9d79002fbacafe741b44416ca02773e2547467e5`:
  - `PROOF_MXC_RUNTIME_EXIT 0`
  - `PROOF_MXC_RUNTIME_STDOUT_BEGIN` included `MXC_RUNTIME_PROOF_OK`
  - `PROOF_MXC_RUNTIME_OK`
  - `PROOF_RUNTIME_AND_SCREENSHOT_COLLECTION_OK`
  - Run summary: `provider=ssh`, `lease=static_172-26-197-87`, `sync=0s`, `command=1m45.849s`, `total=1m46.691s`, `exit=0`.
- Interactive Windows desktop screenshot proof also succeeded:
  - `PROOF_SCREENSHOT_OK`
  - Screenshot SHA256: `410DC677577CB0357904B5D6FA9F202476813ADC565355EB3F40980F758C1B33`
  - Artifact bundle: https://gist.github.com/paulcam206/78a01fef58f5f6d58b3ef0a61737a4df

Native dependency/security surfaces needing maintainer decision:

- Dependency graph changes are intentional for this external plugin:
  - `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`
  - packaged MXC executor binaries from the SDK package
  - `node-pty@1.2.0-beta.13` with install script
  - `pnpm-workspace.yaml` build allowance for `node-pty`
  - root/plugin lock/shrinkwrap changes
- Current `dependency-guard` is expected to fail until a maintainer/admin/secops owner approves the dependency graph. Existing guard output: `Detected 4 dependency-related file change(s). Dependency graph changes require removal or a current admin or secops override.`
- Upstream MXC SDK argv transport is current `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0` behavior, not a local OpenClaw quoting bug:
  - OpenClaw passes its plugin launcher payload via `--payload-file`.
  - The launcher calls `spawnSandboxFromConfig(config, options)`.
  - `@microsoft/mxc-sdk/dist/helper.js` base64-encodes the config envelope and pushes `--config-base64 <base64>` onto the `wxc-exec` argv.
  - `@microsoft/mxc-sdk/dist/sandbox.js` then calls `spawn(executablePath, args, ...)`.
  - Base64 is not secrecy; upstream MXC tracking issue filed: https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/626. Maintainers should explicitly accept that preview-SDK boundary for this prerelease plugin, or pause this PR until the upstream SDK provides a non-argv transport.

Known proof notes:

Fresh export-cleanup validation after removing the stray sandbox barrel export:

- WSL2 fresh clone under `/tmp/openclaw-validate-wsl2`, without using `/mnt/e/repo`:
  - `git diff --check` - passed.
  - `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` - passed.
  - `corepack pnpm test:extension mxc` - passed, 9 files passed / 1 skipped, 65 tests passed / 39 skipped on Linux.
- Windows SSH fresh clone on `adminuser@172.19.169.53` under `C:\Users\adminuser\AppData\Local\Temp\openclaw-validate-win`:
  - `git diff --check` - passed.
  - `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` - passed.
  - `corepack pnpm test:extension mxc` - passed, 10 files passed, 104 tests passed.

- Static Windows proof emitted the MXC host-prep advisory that `C:\` lacks AppContainer directory-listing ACEs. The proof still executed a basic MXC command successfully (`MXC_RUNTIME_PROOF_OK`); the warning is host preparation guidance, not a failure for the proven path.
- Fresh PR CI is running on the pushed head. `dependency-guard` remains the expected maintainer/secops gate.





## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
After the rebase/fixup, the MXC plugin preserves Windows-absolute `mxcBinaryPath` overrides instead of prefixing them with the Linux test runner cwd, and the generated plugin inventory reference is current.

Real environment tested:
Brokered AWS Crabbox Linux source-harness proof from a trusted OpenClaw checkout using `--fresh-pr openclaw/openclaw#97086`, public network, Node `v24.18.0`, pnpm `11.2.2`, and PR head `4c04b33c2c50bae249ea15fe448e2829ce4be0e5`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Verified the remote fresh PR checkout head was exactly `4c04b33c2c50bae249ea15fe448e2829ce4be0e5`.
2. Installed dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
3. Ran `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`.
4. Ran `pnpm plugins:inventory:check`.
5. Ran focused MXC Vitest coverage with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mxc/test/binary-resolver.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/config.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/mxc-backend.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/mxc-spawn-launcher.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/plugin-root.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/plugin.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/readiness.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/sandbox-baseline.test.ts extensions/mxc/test/sandbox-policy-loader.test.ts --reporter=dot`.

Evidence after fix:
Crabbox run `run_dbe60bfb7721` on AWS lease `cbx_950ca1a8cec5` / `violet-krill` completed with exit `0`. The run printed `HEAD=4c04b33c2c50bae249ea15fe448e2829ce4be0e5`, `PROOF_PHASE:static_checks`, `PROOF_PHASE:mxc_tests`, and `PROOF_RESULT:pass`. Vitest reported `8 passed`, `1 skipped`, `63 passed`, `39 skipped`.

Observed result after fix:
The stale plugin inventory check is clean, the Windows-path resolver regression is fixed, and the focused MXC source-harness test set passes on the rebased pushed PR head.

What was not tested:
This rerun was Linux Crabbox source-harness proof for the rebase/fixup regression and generated-doc check. It did not rerun the native Windows MXC runtime path; the existing Windows SSH runtime proof remains recorded above. `dependency-guard` still needs maintainer/admin/secops approval for the new exact head SHA.
